# Normal Dungeon Manastorm cache - candidate mapping

## Target and status

Item 1278050, Manastorm Cache: Normal Dungeons. Exact advertised description:

    Obtained from Manastorm Levels: 1 to 24
    Contains:
    + Normal Dungeon Gear

The user approved using the mapped 611 base items to restore cache 1278050. SQL 49 now implements that targeted CoA reconstruction. Original exact cache membership/odds remain unrecovered; no live database write has been performed.

## Findings

- Reused the 611 explicitly enumerated ClassicDungeonCatalog base IDs already preserved in SQL 26.
- All 611 IDs exist in the refreshed item dump and are equippable weapons/armor.
- Every base item has ItemLevel=57; RequiredLevel ranges from 46 through 60.
- 600 are rare (Quality=3); 11 are epic (Quality=4).
- No @Normal Dungeon@ tagged alternative was found among matching names, or globally in the scanned item rows.
- The base items are therefore the candidate Normal-tier IDs. This is a strong reconstruction from the historical catalogue, item-level pattern and separate ranked variants, not an original per-cache loot capture.
- 586 IDs also appear in AtlasLoot Classic Instances.lua records whose reference is represented by the ClassicInstances.lua menu. The other 25 lack that corroboration in this inspected AtlasLoot snapshot.
- Some names have multiple unranked rows. Exact catalogue base IDs resolve identity without picking arbitrary same-name duplicates. In particular, use catalogue ID 22301 for Ironweave Robe; do not add same-name 2230111 merely because it exists.
- A level-60 realm's gear need not require exactly character level 60. RequiredLevel and ItemLevel are different fields. These candidates have endgame Normal item level 57, while their required levels remain 46-60.

## Evidence and limitations

[Existing SQL 26](../data/sql/db-world/base/26_manastorm_cache_molten_core_full_reconstruction.sql) preserves the explicit base IDs and documents their origin in a historical Mythic+ reward-name catalogue, including UBRS. That original catalogue establishes dungeon reward candidates; extending its base IDs to this Normal cache remains reconstruction.

[Ascension AtlasLoot Classic item data](https://github.com/Szyler/AtlasLootAscension/blob/master/AtlasLoot/Databases/Items/Classic/Instances.lua), blob dd69a91b91e79c7056c78669ee1e2b8e7471d407, says it was auto-generated from Ascension DB. Its [menu](https://github.com/Szyler/AtlasLootAscension/blob/master/AtlasLoot/UI/Menus/ClassicInstances.lua), blob 0be89e11d314385cc5c3a6fc0a56fdcd4f3bf5ff, supplies source-reference labels. Dungeon membership and Mythic reward membership do not individually prove Normal cache inclusion.

The [official Chapter 2 reward table](https://ascension.gg/de/news/chapter-2-pre-patch-updates/461) confirms the Normal cache starts at depth 1 and Heroic at depth 25. It does not provide a complete per-item loot list or roll odds.

The current export's 207 level-80 items in 1278050 are unsuitable for the Classic policy. Do not append the candidate list to that wrong pool. Any restoration must replace only the targeted cache rows and preserve other containers.

## Complete machine-readable inventory

[NORMAL_DUNGEON_CACHE_CANDIDATES.csv](NORMAL_DUNGEON_CACHE_CANDIDATES.csv) contains every candidate ID, exact name, item metadata, evidence classification and item-dump line. Its 611 rows are an inventory of candidates, not claimed recovered original cache membership.

## Restoration migration

[49_manastorm_classic_normal_dungeon_cache.sql](../data/sql/db-world/base/49_manastorm_classic_normal_dungeon_cache.sql) replaces only item_loot_template rows for cache 1278050 with the 611 explicit base IDs above. The 25 historical-catalogue-only entries are included in the approved reconstruction. The prior 207 level-80 candidates are removed from this cache.

It retains one equal-choice group (Chance=0, GroupId=1, MinCount=MaxCount=1) and the existing primary-stat preference hook. This is a CoA policy choice, not recovered original probabilities. Heroic cache 1278051, other caches, item templates, reference pools, conditions, brackets and player progression are not written.

Preflight requires the existing item_manastorm_cache binding, HAS_LOOT, an InnoDB item loot table, all 611 exact candidate identities/metadata, item level 57, required levels at most 60, and no existing loot conditions on this cache. Failure raises an error and rolls back before replacing loot. The migration uses a temporary procedure and requires CREATE ROUTINE permission, matching the SQL 26 pattern.

Apply SQL 49 to acore_world and restart worldserver to load the new item loot. No C++ rebuild or character SQL is needed for this data-only change. Expected post-write query: 611 distinct candidates, item level 57, required levels 46-60. Migration is prepared, not applied to the live database.

Validation: generated candidate rows and mutation/predicate SQL exercised in a SQLite data model; exact IDs, targeted replacement, unchanged unrelated cache rows and repeat application passed. Missing candidates, changed metadata/levels and existing conditions are rejected by the predicate model. MySQL stored-procedure execution and in-game opening were not tested. Formatting/safety checks passed except the existing backtick checker falsely flags COUNT, BINARY and SIGNAL's MESSAGE_TEXT keywords; SQL identifiers are quoted.

# Heroic Dungeon Manastorm cache restoration

## Target and advertised intent

Item 1278051, Manastorm Cache: Heroic Dungeons. The exported description is:

    Obtained from Manastorm Levels: 25 to 105
    Contains:
    + Normal Dungeon Gear
    + Heroic Dungeon Gear

The exported pool contains 1480 candidates requiring level 80. [SQL 50](../data/sql/db-world/base/50_manastorm_classic_heroic_dungeon_cache.sql) replaces this cache's loot rows and creates two dedicated tier pools with the mapped Classic Normal and Heroic tiers.

## Mapping

The same 611 base IDs used in SQL 49 provide the Normal tier: item level 57, RequiredLevel 46-60, 600 rare and 11 epic items. Their original membership evidence and caveats remain documented in [NORMAL_DUNGEON_CACHE_MAPPING.md](NORMAL_DUNGEON_CACHE_MAPPING.md).

Each has exactly one selected Heroic counterpart with matching exact name, class, subclass, equipment slot and display model. All 611 Heroic items have item level 61, RequiredLevel 60 and epic quality (4). 610 have an explicit @Heroic Dungeon@ description prefix.

One explicit exception: base 23198 Idol of Brutality maps to Heroic 323198, described @Heroic@. Its name, class 4/subclass 8, slot 28, display 28174, required level 60, quality 4 and item level 61 all match the Heroic tier. Its separately named Mythic/raid/ranked variants were not substituted. This legacy marker mapping is a documented reconstruction rather than a guessed ID.

The combined pool has 1222 unique existing item IDs. [HEROIC_DUNGEON_CACHE_CANDIDATES.csv](HEROIC_DUNGEON_CACHE_CANDIDATES.csv) records each ID, tier, base relationship, exact description, metadata and dump line.

## Selection policy

The source description establishes both gear families, but does not establish original quantities or probabilities. User-approved CoA policy is one guaranteed item: 75% Heroic and 25% Normal. These are reconstruction odds, not recovered Ascension odds.

Two explicit-chance reference rows share GroupId=1: Heroic reference 9003002 has Chance=75, Normal reference 9003001 has Chance=25. Each reference contains 611 pure gear candidates in an equal-choice group. The core selects the tier before invoking existing primary-stat personalization on that tier's leaf pool; stat weights do not change the tier split.

The scoped OnAfterRefCount guard in ManastormCacheLoot.cpp forces one reference iteration for cache 1278051 and these two references while the module is enabled. This prevents global Rate.Drop.Item.ReferencedAmount from changing the reward count. Other caches and reference pools retain their existing behavior.

## Migration safeguards and scope

Preflight requires item_manastorm_cache ownership, HAS_LOOT, InnoDB item and reference loot, all 1222 exact candidate identities and captured tier metadata/descriptions, RequiredLevel at most 60, and no item-loot conditions attached to 1278051. A mismatch raises an error and rolls back rather than installing a partial pool.

Normal cache 1278050, other containers, item templates, conditions, brackets and player progression are not written. Reserved references 9003001/9003002 are checked for ownership, external consumers across all loot stores, and reference conditions before transactional writes. Both loot tables must use InnoDB. Reapplication preserves the same two owned pools.

SQL 50 embeds both tiers and does not require SQL 49. SQL 20 ownership must already be present. CREATE ROUTINE permission is required. Rebuild the changed module, apply SQL 50 to acore_world, and restart worldserver. Expected query output: two root rows with 75/25 chances, 611 candidates in each reference pool. No live SQL was executed.

## Validation

Checked all 1222 generated candidate tuples against the saved candidate CSV, with 611 unique items per tier and no overlap. Deterministic enumeration of 10,000 tier rolls selects Heroic 7500 times and Normal 2500 times. Varying within-tier stat weights leaves those tier totals unchanged. Each leaf item has MinCount=MaxCount=1 and the scoped guard forces one iteration for zero, fractional and increased global reference amount rates.

Verified grouped-reference processing, shared Loot/container GUID propagation, equal-choice hook behavior, and the exact OnAfterRefCount signature and enabled-hook enum against this branch's core source. Existing identity/metadata/condition preflight checks are retained. Reserved namespace searches found no existing 9003001/9003002 pools in the supplied loot export or local module evidence.

The earlier direct-pool predicate model checks established rejection of missing items, changed tier metadata and existing cache conditions. The new tier mutation was exercised in a SQLite data model: 611 leaves per pool, exclusive 75/25 root group, unchanged Normal cache, and idempotent reapplication passed. The guard was checked separately. MySQL stored-procedure execution, C++ compilation and in-game opening were not tested.

## SQL 50 temporary-table compatibility fix

The initial SQL 50 tier-count IF referenced tmp_ms_heroic_candidate twice in one statement, causing MySQL error 1137 before persistent loot writes. Both counts now come from one conditional-aggregate SELECT into procedure-local variables. All candidate-table statements use a single reference. The failed invocation reaches neither persistent DELETE nor INSERT; rerun the complete corrected SQL 50, which recreates its temporary table and procedure.

Conditional counts were checked against the 1222 candidate tuples and missing-tier/empty fixtures in SQLite. Full MySQL procedure execution remains untested. See [MySQL temporary-table restrictions](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/temporary-table-problems.html).

# Classic Mythic Dungeon cache 1278054

The supplied item export names this item Manastorm Cache: Mythic Dungeons and describes it as:

> Manastorm 201 to 250
> Contains gear up to Mythic Dungeons!

The supplied loot export has no loot rows or references for this cache. It is a scriptless HAS_LOOT container,
RequiredLevel 60, with no recovered item-loot conditions. This describes the export, not a live database query.

## Candidate mapping

[MYTHIC_DUNGEON_CACHE_CANDIDATES.csv](MYTHIC_DUNGEON_CACHE_CANDIDATES.csv) records 1833 unique item IDs,
their exact descriptions, metadata, source lines and base relationships: 611 Normal, 611 Heroic and 611 Mythic.
The Normal and Heroic tiers reuse the documented SQL 49/50 mappings and their reconstruction caveats.
Each Mythic variant matches its base name, class, subclass, equipment slot and display model exactly.
All 611 Mythic variants have the exact description @Mythic Dungeon@, epic quality and RequiredLevel 60.
No @Mythic 1@, @Mythic 2@ or other ranked Mythic+ variants are included.

610 Mythic items have ItemLevel 64. The explicit exception is 523198, Idol of Brutality, ItemLevel 70,
mapped from base 23198. Its plain Mythic Dungeon description and identity are retained; item level alone
is not a tier classifier. Normal items have ItemLevel 57; Heroic items have ItemLevel 61.

## User-approved selection policy

One guaranteed item while the module is enabled: 75% Mythic, 20% Heroic, 5% Normal. These are CoA policy odds,
not recovered Ascension odds. Three explicit-chance root rows share GroupId 1, selecting exactly one tier.
Dedicated reference pools 9003101 (Normal), 9003102 (Heroic) and 9003103 (Mythic) each contain 611 pure gear
leaves. Existing primary-stat preference applies after tier selection and does not alter the tier split.

ManastormRewards recognizes 1278054 even outside the active depth catalogue, allowing existing or granted
copies to use stat preference. The existing OnAfterRefCount guard now also covers this cache's three pools,
forcing one reference iteration regardless of global reference amount rates. Standard container opening,
Normal and Heroic cache behavior, Mode 1/2 transport, depth brackets and progression remain unchanged.

## Migration and validation

Apply SQL 53 to acore_world after rebuilding the changed module, then restart worldserver. Its preflight
checks the scriptless HAS_LOOT cache, all 1833 exact candidate identities and descriptions, level at most 60,
InnoDB loot tables, conditions, and reserved-reference ownership/consumers across all loot stores.
Persistent loot changes are transactional. Tier counts use one temporary-table reference per statement,
avoiding the MySQL error 1137 encountered in the initial SQL 50.

SQLite model checks passed for generated candidate identity, 611 leaves per tier, actual migration mutation,
75/20/5 exclusive root group, unchanged Heroic cache and idempotent reapplication. Missing-tier and empty
fixtures fail the count checks. All Mythic candidates were verified to have the exact unranked marker.
MySQL procedure execution, C++ compilation and in-game opening remain untested.

# Dedicated Classic ranked dungeon cache restoration

SQL 61 restores four scriptless HAS_LOOT containers, all empty in the supplied loot export.
It embeds four independent gear pools and is self-contained; previous cache migrations are not prerequisites.
These four caches were outside SQL 47's historical Classic award catalogue. The selected S9-based S10 progression
now activates them through `zzzz_rev_20261025_100_manastorm_s9_classic_cache_progression.sql`. Restoration does not activate them,
change brackets or replace any current raid cache rewards. Existing/manual copies can use their loot.

## Exported descriptions and selected reconstruction policy

| Cache | Exported depth | Selected gear band | Candidates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1278059 Mythic 1-10 | 501-550 | Dungeon ranks 1-10 | 6109 |
| 1278064 Mythic 11-20 | 751-800 | Dungeon ranks 11-20 | 6110 |
| 1278073 Mythic 21-30 | 1301-1350 | Dungeon ranks 21-30 | 6110 |
| 1278082 Mythic 31-40 | 1851-1900 | Dungeon ranks 31-40 | 6110 |

Each opening selects one item from the named band, personalized by the existing stat preference.
This is a CoA reconstruction policy. The wording 'up to' establishes a ceiling, but does not establish
original lower-tier mixing, tier probabilities, quantities or exact cache membership. No lower-band,
plain Mythic, raid or Ascended items are added under this policy. Candidate metadata and rank identity
are supported by the supplied item export and the previously reviewed Classic dungeon catalogue.
Exported depths are historical evidence; see MANASTORM_CLASSIC_CACHE_UNLOCKS.md for the current selected progression.

Exact descriptions:

    Manastorm 501 to 550
    Contains gear up to Mythic 1-10!

    1278073

## Mapping evidence and gap

The saved Normal Dungeon mapping supplies 611 Classic dungeon equipment base identities from the
Ascension-specific AtlasLoot catalogue. Ranked variants match base name, class, subclass, equipment slot
and display model, require at most level 60, have epic quality and carry the exact advertised rank prefix.
Same-name raid and higher-level variants are excluded. Existing rank 11-40 mappings are reused from the
BWL/AQ/Naxx restorations; ranks 1-10 reuse SQL 26's identity rule and ambiguity exclusion.

One unresolved identity: base 22253 Tome of the Lost at Mythic +3 has two exact-name/model/slot matches:

| Item ID | Item level | Exact description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8263152 | 71 | @Mythic 3@The title reads "The Brode to Nowhere" |
| 8263154 | 66 | @Mythic 3@The title reads "The Brode to Nowhere" |

Both are excluded rather than guessing the intended variant. Rank 3 has 610 candidates; every other
rank 1-40 has 611. There are no other gaps or equally preferred ambiguities in the selected mapping.
Each candidate is a configured item ID, not an additional item per opening.

[RANKED_DUNGEON_CACHE_CANDIDATES.csv](RANKED_DUNGEON_CACHE_CANDIDATES.csv) records all assignments,
base relationships, exact descriptions, metadata, item-export line numbers and explicit ranks.

## Runtime and migration

Each cache has one explicit 100% root group referencing one pure gear band. The scoped OnAfterRefCount
guard preserves one selected item regardless of global reference amount rates while the module is enabled.
Existing stat preference selects within that pool. The four cache IDs are recognized outside active
brackets so already-owned or manually granted copies retain personalized opening.

SQL 61 owns only roots 1278059/1278064/1278073/1278082 and references 9003801-9003804. It does not update
items, scripts, names/descriptions, depth brackets, progression, other loot pools or Mode 1/2 transport.
Preflight checks InnoDB loot tables, four scriptless HAS_LOOT containers, all 24439 captured item
assignments and their exact metadata, four pool counts, namespace ownership, external consumers across
all loot stores and existing loot conditions. Persistent changes are transactional and idempotent.
Each temporary table appears once per statement, avoiding MySQL 1137.

Rebuild the module, apply SQL 61 to acore_world, then restart worldserver. CREATE ROUTINE permission is
required. No live database write was performed. Previous cache migrations do not need rerunning.

## Validation

SQLite checks passed for all 24439 generated SQL/CSV tuples and exact metadata, four pool counts,
rank-band boundaries and the +3 ambiguity exclusion, four guaranteed one-item root groups, repeat
application and preservation of unrelated Naxx rows. The actual metadata predicate rejected wrong
descriptions, level-80 gear, changed display models and wrong quality. The four-container preflight was
checked. Memberships match reviewed SQL 26 and the BWL/AQ40/Naxx CSVs. Formatting and single temporary-table
references were checked.
SQL formatting, quoting, insert/delete safety and engine checks passed; the directory check flags the
intentional module base migration. C++ checks passed except for pre-existing blank-line warnings in
ManastormRewards.cpp, confirmed unchanged against HEAD.
MySQL procedure execution, C++ compilation and in-game openings remain untested.
